hook.line: Every travel chat in Colombia has the same shape. The first question asks if you've ever been; the moment you say yes, the next one asks when. Spanish switches past forms right at that moment.
hook.es:
¿Has estado en Cartagena?
Sí, fui el año pasado.
hook.en:
Have you been to Cartagena?
Yes, I went last year.

examples.es:
¿Has estado en Medellín?
Sí, dos veces.
examples.en:
Have you been to Medellín?
Yes, twice.
When did you go? (to a friend)

examples.es: Fui en diciembre con mi familia.
examples.en: I went in December with my family.

examples.es: Todavía no he ido a Leticia.
examples.en: I haven't been to Leticia yet.

examples.es: He montado a caballo una vez.
Monté a caballo el año pasado en Villa de Leyva.
examples.en: I rode a horse last year in Villa de Leyva.

rule:
Two different questions, two different forms.

Whether, at any point in your life: *he*, *has*, *ha*. *¿Has estado en Cartagena?* *Nunca he ido a Leticia.*

When, where, who with, how it was: the plain past. *¿Cuándo fuiste?* *Fui en diciembre.*

So a yes flips the conversation. *¿Has estado en Medellín?* *Sí, fui el año pasado.* The first line is about your life; the answer is about one trip.

English does the same: nobody says I've been there last year. Spanish is just as strict. A finished time (*ayer*, *en 2019*, *el año pasado*, *en diciembre*) always means the plain past. Ever, never, twice, not yet: *he*.
smallPrint: Teachers call these the present perfect (*pretérito perfecto*) and the preterite (*pretérito indefinido*).

yourTurn.prompt: Pick and type the whole sentence: *¿___ en Cartagena?* (*Has estado* or *Estuviste*) Asking a friend if she's ever been.
yourTurn.why: Ever, at any point in her life: *has estado*.

yourTurn.prompt: Pick and type the whole sentence: *Sí, ___ el año pasado.* (*he ido* or *fui*) Yes, I went last year.
yourTurn.why: *El año pasado* is a finished time, so the plain past.

yourTurn.prompt: Your friend says she's been to Medellín. Ask her: When did you go?
yourTurn.why: Asking when is about one trip, so the plain past.

yourTurn.prompt: Say: I've been to Medellín twice.
yourTurn.answer: He estado en Medellín dos veces.
accept: He estado dos veces en Medellín.
He ido a Medellín dos veces.
yourTurn.why: Twice in your life, no date: *he estado*.

yourTurn.prompt: Say: I went to Medellín in December.
Ask Don Hernando, politely: Have you been to Cartagena?
Add a date: *He montado a caballo.* Make it I rode a horse last year.
yourTurn.answer: Monté a caballo el año pasado.
accept: El año pasado monté a caballo.
yourTurn.why: Once there's a finished time, *he montado* becomes the plain past *monté*.

pitfalls.wrong: He ido a Cartagena el año pasado.
pitfalls.right: Fui a Cartagena el año pasado.
pitfalls.why: Almost. A finished time like *el año pasado* takes the plain past, just as English drops I've.
Asking when is about one trip, so use the plain past.

pitfalls.wrong:
¿Has estado en Medellín?
Sí, he ido en diciembre.
pitfalls.right:
¿Has estado en Medellín?
Sí, fui en diciembre.
pitfalls.why: The question is about your life, but the answer names a month: switch to the plain past.

personal: Pick a place you've been. Write one line saying you've been there (*he estado*), then one saying when you went (*fui*).
